story.text: Tell me about a time you had to fix a {part} on {a_item}.
Tell me about the first {item} you ever saw.
How did you look after {a_item} so that it lasted?
Tell me about a day when {a_item} made all the difference.
Who showed you how to use {a_item}, and what did they say?
What did you like best about the {part} on {a_item}?
Tell me about the {item} you knew best.
Tell me how you made {a_item} the way you liked it.
Tell me what you grew, and how you looked after your {item_pl}.
Tell me about a day you spent at {the_item}.
Tell me about playing {the_item}, and who played with you.
What do you think is the secret to looking after {a_item}?
What is it about {item_pl} that people never grow tired of?
If you were showing a young person about {item_pl}, where would you begin?
What would you look for when choosing {a_item}?
Which part of {a_item} do you think matters most: the {part} or the {part2}?
What did people love most about {item_pl} in {decade}?

open.text: What do you think made {a_item} so {praise}?
Why do you think people kept {item_pl} for so many years?
If you could change one thing about {a_item}, what would it be?
How would you describe {a_item} to someone who has never seen one?
What would you say is the best thing about {a_item}?
What would you look for if you were picking {a_item} for {outing}?
What sight, sound or feeling goes with {a_item}?
If you were designing {a_item} today, what would you add?
Who do you think would enjoy {a_item} most, and why?
Why do you think {item_pl} have been loved for so long?
What do you think the {part} does for {a_item}?
Where would {a_item} feel most at home?

pair.text: Which would you choose for {outing}: {a_item} or {a_item2}? What makes you say so?
What do {item_pl} and {item2_pl} have in common?
Which do you think is more useful: {a_item} or {a_item2}? Why?
Which one would make a place feel more lively: {a_item} or {a_item2}?

factFollow: What do you make of that?
What does that bring to mind?
What would you add to that?
How does that sound to you?

intro: Finish each thought. The word you need is in the box.
Choose a word from the box to finish each one. Any word that fits is a good one.
Read each one and finish it with a word from the box.

sight.text: Look at the {color} color of this {item}.

anchor.text: Take a slow breath. Look at {the_item}.

instructions.wordsearch.early: Circle each word. Words can go across, down and slanted.
instructions.wordsearch.middle: Circle each word. Words go across and down.
instructions.wordsearch.late: Find the word. Point to it, or circle it.
instructions.talk.early: Talk about it, or write on the lines. Every answer is welcome.
instructions.puzzle.early: Each word fits one of the spaces. Use the clues and the box of words.
instructions.puzzle.middle: Each word fits one of the spaces. The first letter is already there.
instructions.puzzle.late: Look at this together. Take as long as you like.
instructions.coloring.early: Color it any way you like.
instructions.coloring.middle: Color it any way you like.
instructions.coloring.late: Any colors you like. Any way you like.
instructions.staff.note: Pages 1 to 4 are for the resident. This page is for staff: take it off before handing the packet over.

early: over a cup of tea or coffee
when you sit down together after lunch
during a quiet part of the afternoon
on the walk to the activity room
while you tidy up after a meal
middle: when you sit together after lunch
during the calm part of the afternoon
as you walk together to the activity room
while you set the table together
late: as you sit beside {them} in the morning
at the start of a meal
when you sit down together after lunch
during the quiet part of the afternoon
as you settle {them} in for the evening
when you pull your chair close

templates.text: {name}'s own name is hidden in the word search on Page 1. Point to it first; it is usually the word people spot right away.
On Page 1, say the word {word} out loud and let {name} look for it at {their} own pace.
On Page 1, circle one word together, then step back and let {name} choose the next one.
Hold Page 1 where {name} can see it. Say the word {word}, then trace its letters slowly with your finger.
{Moment}, ask {them} about {the_item} on Page 2. Let {them} lead; a single sentence is plenty.
{Moment}, wonder aloud about {the_item} from Page 2, and follow wherever {they} take the conversation.
Read the first thought on Page 2 aloud, then pause. If {they_finish} it, repeat it back warmly; if not, point to the box of words.
{Moment}, hold Page 2 where {they} can see it and read one card slowly. Then wait: silence is part of the conversation.
Bring up {the_item} from Page {page} {moment}, and let {them} take it wherever {they} like.
{Moment}, say a few words about {the_item} from Page {page}. A smile or a glance is an answer too.
If the crossword on Page 3 feels like too much, read one clue aloud and point to the box of words. Finishing is not the goal.
On Page 3, read a clue aloud and point to the matching word in the box. The first letters are already filled in to help.
Page 3 shows {the_item}. Hold it in {their} line of sight, say what it is, and let {them} look for as long as {they} would like.
Offer two or three bold markers for Page 4 and let {name} choose. Staying inside the lines does not matter.
Page 4 is a pattern to color. Place a marker in {their} hand and make the first stroke together if {they} would like.
If {they_seem} restless, talk quietly about {the_item} from Page {page} and describe {sense_cue}.
Afterward, note anything {name} enjoyed, such as a smile, a story or a single word, in today's engagement notes.
If any page seems to upset {name}, set it aside and sit quietly together. Nothing here needs to be finished.
